authority_note: Routing is deterministic code bound to this policy version. Every routing decision records policy_version so it can be re-derived. Changing any threshold requires a policy_version bump.

minimum_quality_floor.note: §91. Applied BEFORE cost ranking, never after. A weaker model is never chosen merely because it is cheaper.

bootstrap.problem: With the cold-start posterior (prior 0.75, weight 8) and an empty ledger, no pair can reach 0.96 or 0.99. Taken literally the floor blocks all HIGH and CRITICAL work on day one -- a self-blocking gate.
bootstrap.inherit_note: A pair whose model+harness matches a DEC-028 worker card that was already QUALIFIED inherits that card's qualification as its floor basis, because that exact pairing already carried production authority. This grandfathers claude-code+claude-sonnet-5 and codex-app-server+gpt-5.6-sol and nothing else.
bootstrap.uninherited_note: A pair with no inherited qualification and no ledger evidence may take LOW and MEDIUM work only. It reaches HIGH/CRITICAL by accumulating trusted-outcome evidence, never by assertion.
bootstrap.expires_when: the ledger holds sufficient trusted-outcome samples for the pair at the requested risk class

minimum_quality_floor.high_risk_never_first_test_note: §65. An unproven model's first DIAL execution may not be a HIGH or CRITICAL task.

cost_model.note: §14's denominator adds token_cost + latency + expected_rework_cost, which sums tokens, milliseconds and rework -- three different units. §55 separately introduces effective_execution_cost without connecting it back. This policy resolves the two into one normalised function.
cost_model.subscription_note: §55. Flat-rate access, rolling quotas, seat limits and rate limits mean scarcity pressure can matter more than nominal token price.

behavioural_guidance_budgets.note: The document states three budget tables. §23 (routine 100 / moderate 200 / complex 400) conflicts with §50 and §87, which agree with each other. The two-against-one agreement is adopted; §23 is treated as superseded. These limits are ENFORCEABLE (§87), not advisory, and cover model-specific behavioural guidance ONLY -- never required engineering context.
behavioural_guidance_budgets.none_note: §24/§50. ModelExecutionProfile = NONE is a valid and expected result when no model-specific adaptation is expected to improve the outcome.

token_accounting.note: §87 makes budgets enforceable and §89/§101 require per-source token counts, but the document never says whose tokenizer. Claude and GPT tokenize the same text to different counts, so a single number cannot be correct for both.
token_accounting.enforcement_note: Budgets are enforced against the estimate inflated by the error bound, so an under-estimate cannot silently exceed a hard limit. Where a harness exposes an exact token count, the exact count supersedes the estimate and the margin is dropped.

hysteresis.note: §59. Small routing-score changes must not cause mid-task churn.
hysteresis.bypass_note: ESCALATION_STOP_LOSS is added to resolve a deadlock the document leaves open: §92 demands escalation after repeated similar failures, while §59 blocks a switch whose score improvement is below threshold. Failure-driven escalation therefore outranks hysteresis.

degraded_mode.note: §75. A simple documentation task may fall back; production credential rotation blocks if no qualified route exists.

conservative_routing_under_weak_telemetr.note: §97. Unknown models may be tested under low-risk or shadow conditions, never assumed equal to qualified routes.

subscription_capacity.note: Not specified in the document. §55 names subscription limits and §77 names concurrency, but nothing connects them: parallel workers can both route to the same premium model and both stall on one rate limit. Capacity is therefore reserved the way compute-governor.mjs already reserves tokens.

reviewer_independence.note: §63. Reuses the independence_class diversity already implemented in harness-capability-exchange.mjs rather than introducing a second mechanism.
